correctness.rationale: After k rounds distances to the two named vertices are visible. Counts of adjacent vertices simultaneously closer to both and farther from both yield z(a-t) and t(c-z). Their difference equals a(p+q-k)+(2k-n)t. When n>2k this determines the remaining zone count t; when n=2k its quadratic equation identifies precisely the complement-permutation involution. Exhibited marked-point automorphisms act transitively within each resulting class. Coefficient enumeration and Burnside give counts. Two independently written finite programs corroborate formula and partitions; they do not replace the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The stable partition of an entire two-anchor Johnson family is a natural exact orbit invariant, with a combinatorial coefficient class count, explicit binomial class sizes, a sharp complement-symmetry transition and a uniform k+1 round bound. A genuine local count is required beyond the two anchor distances, connecting symmetry with logical expressivity. It is not a parameter-only renaming or a known-table recomputation; its scope is explicitly k>=3.
